logline.en: A con artist opens the bag she has just stolen and finds a ringing phone instead of forty lakh rupees. The man on the line knows her real name, and tells her to ask her own driver who he is working for tonight.

story.location: Back seat of a kaali-peeli (black-and-yellow) taxi parked under a concrete flyover in a Mumbai-like city. Rain running down the windows, sodium-orange street light, red and blue neon from a shuttered shop smeared across wet glass. Engine off.

characters.role: LEAD. Con artist. Tonight she played 'Nisha', a private-bank relationship manager.
characters.look: Indian woman, 31, lean, sharp cheekbones, warm brown skin. Shoulder-length black hair, damp from rain, left side tucked behind the ear. Small gold stud in the left nostril. Smudged kajal. Thin gold chain at the collarbone. Charcoal fitted blazer, wet at the shoulders, over a maroon silk blouse: her bank-officer disguise. No other jewellery, short unpainted nails. Same face, hair, nose stud, blazer and blouse in every shot.
characters.note: Same voice as the Hinglish cut. Late 20s to early 30s female, urban Mumbai Indian English, quick and low, a little husky. Starts the scene high on adrenaline and laughing; by the end she is barely above a whisper. Never shrill. Not British, not American.

characters.role: Her driver and partner of six years. Seen mostly as eyes in the rear-view mirror and the back of his head.
characters.look: Indian man, 46, heavy-lidded tired eyes, salt-and-pepper stubble, thick greying hair cut short. Faded khaki taxi-driver shirt, sleeves rolled, steel kada on the right wrist. Broad shoulders filling the driver's seat.
characters.note: Same voice as the Hinglish cut. Mid-40s male, working-class Mumbai Indian English with a clear Hindi accent, gravelly and unhurried. Short plain sentences, says very little. Flat and tired, never raises his voice; the last line is a sigh, not a threat.

characters.role: The man she robbed tonight. Voice on the phone only.
characters.note: Same voice as the Hinglish cut. About 60, male, cultured old-money South Bombay English, precise, soft and amused, unhurried but never drawling. Does not use contractions. Sounds like he is smiling. His last line (l08) drops lower and slower but stays fully voiced: never a whisper, every word clear. Phone-filtered in the mix (narrow band, slight line hiss).

endingQuestion.hi: इमरान ने दरवाज़े lock किए: तारा को सौंपने के लिए, या बचाने के लिए?
endingQuestion.en: Imran locked the doors: to hand Tara over, or to protect her?

beats.action: Open inside the moment. Tight on TARA in the back seat, still wired from the job, rain-damp, laughing, a tan leather duffel bag on her lap, both hands on the zip and already starting to pull it as she speaks. IMRAN is only a pair of eyes in the rear-view mirror. Engine off, wipers still, rain drumming on the roof.

She rips the zip open. Insert, top-down into the bag: no cash. Neat bundles of cut newspaper held with rubber bands, and on top of them one cheap black keypad phone. Back to Tara's face: the grin dies where it is.

The keypad phone lights up in the bag and rings, harsh and far too loud in the closed car. Its green glow lands on Tara's face from below. She stares at it. Her thumb moves towards the answer key. Imran's eyes snap to her in the mirror.

She answers anyway. Close on Tara in profile, the cheap phone at her ear, rain streaking the window behind her, neon bleeding red and blue through the drops. The CALLER is voice only. She tries to bluff; he talks straight over her.

Tara has stopped breathing. Slow push in on her face, front on, eyes wide and fixed on nothing. Out of focus in the foreground, the back of Imran's head has not moved. On the caller's last word the line goes dead.

Silence except rain and a dead-line tone. Tara lowers the phone a few centimetres. Her eyes travel up to the rear-view mirror. Imran's eyes are already there, watching her. His hand moves on the door panel. CLUNK: all four door locks drop. Tara's hand, on the door handle, stops.

Behind the taxi a parked car's headlights switch on, flooding the cabin white through the rear window and turning Tara into a rim-lit silhouette, the dead phone still in her hand. Imran does not turn around. Optional insert, same mirror set-up as b6: his eyes go from Tara to that light and stay on it a moment, and it must not be clear whether he is signalling the car behind or afraid of it. Then he turns the key and the engine catches (sound only, no wiper). Hold on Tara's face under his last line, then cut to black.

problems: VERDICT: pass, no fatal problem. Sub-scores: hook in first 5 s 7.5, stakes 8, cliffhanger 8.5, natural Hinglish 7.5, performability with tags 7.5, length 7, lead coverage 9.5. Checked by script: JSON is valid, emotion_tags match the inline tags on all 10 lines, spoken 24.5 s + silent 6.0 s = 30.5 s as claimed, Tara is on screen in 7 of 7 beats, 3 characters (one voice-only). File: <repo>/content/proof/photoreal/script.hi.json

HINGLISH, must fix: bookish pronouns. l03 uses 'यह' twice and l08 uses 'वह'. Nobody in Mumbai or UP says 'yah/vah' in speech; they say 'ये/वो'. Plan section 2 says the written text is exactly what the voice reads and what the subtitle shows, so the voice may say 'vah' in the single most important line of the scene.

LENGTH: the per-line targets are optimistic, so the real cut will run about 33 to 35 s, not 30.5. The caller is directed as 'completely unhurried' yet has the densest lines: l07 at 12 characters per second and l08 at 13.1, against 9 to 10 for everyone else. l08 also carries an ellipsis pause and a whispered second half. b7 packs ignition, wiper sweep, headlights, a hold on her face and a cut to black into 3.3 s. This is my estimate from line density, not a measured take.

PERFORMABILITY, key line at risk: the second half of l08 is the ending question itself, and it is whispered, band-limited by the phone filter, and sits over a heavy rain bed plus drone. Whispered Hindi through a narrow-band filter is the likeliest line in the scene to come out unintelligible.

PIPELINE COVERAGE and Hinglish density: only 4 Latin-script words in 3 of 10 lines (Bag, Wrong number, driver). Tara is described as 'Mumbai Hindi with easy English' but has one English phrase. Section 7.1 names timing and pronunciation on mixed Devanagari + Latin lines as the highest-risk unknown, and this proof scene barely exercises it. It also reads closer to plain Hindi than to how a 31-year-old Mumbai con artist talks.
CRAFT: l03 ('what is this?') is generic filler. The insert shot of cut newspaper already says it, and it is the weakest line in an otherwise tight script.

HOOK: the first 4.7 s are celebration and set-up (l01, l02). The actual shock, the empty bag and the phone, lands at roughly 6 to 8 s. The opening works on irony and Imran's planted 'पहले गिन लो', which is good, but it is not the strongest possible first 5 seconds for a scroll format.

CLIFFHANGER, minor: the stated ending_question ('who is Imran driving for tonight?') is spoken aloud by the caller and then largely answered by the lock, the callback line and the tail-car headlights. What is genuinely open is whether Imran is delivering her or protecting her. The triple button risks over-confirming betrayal and losing that ambiguity, and the ending_question field does not name the real open question.

CONTINUITY: Tara is 'still out of breath from running' but the taxi is parked with engine off and wipers still, and the caller says she became Nisha 'आज शाम' while the scene is at about 2 am. The gap between the evening con and a just-now bag grab is unexplained. Small, but an attentive viewer will feel it.

TAGS: l04 '[urgent]' contradicts Imran's voice note ('flat and tired, never raises his voice'). l09 stacks two tags on a one-word line, which is where tagged speech models are least stable. '[cold]' and '[deadpan]' are less common directions and are unverified on the chosen model; I did not test them.

STILLS-ONLY STAGING (section 9: no image-to-video): b6 and b7 describe about seven motion events in 6.7 s (eyes travel, hand moves, locks drop, hand stops, key turns, wiper sweeps, headlights switch on). Several can only exist as sound. b4 holds one set-up for 8.5 s, above the 8 s ceiling in section 7.3, while b2, b3 and b6 imply shots of about 1.2 to 1.7 s.

MINOR: (a) the 'language' field starts with 'hi-Latn-mixed', which literally means Hindi in Latin script, the opposite of the convention used; wrong if any tool parses it or passes it as language_code. (b) Central locking that drops all four doors in an old-engine kaali-peeli is a small authenticity stretch; low priority, the sound moment is worth keeping.

look.summary: Photoreal, cinematic, fictional Indian cast. Night, monsoon, Mumbai-like city. Crime/con tone (Series 1).
look.styleBlock: STYLE: Photorealistic live-action film still, a single frame from a contemporary Indian crime thriller shot on a full-frame digital cinema camera. Vertical 9:16 portrait composition. Night, about 2 am, heavy monsoon rain, inside an old black-and-yellow city taxi parked under a concrete flyover in a Mumbai-like city. Real-looking fictional Indian people with natural, un-retouched skin: visible pores, fine lines, a damp sheen, no beauty smoothing. Lighting is motivated and low-key only: warm sodium-orange street light (about 2000 K) through the rain-streaked windscreen from the front right is the key; red and blue neon from a shuttered shop on the kerb side, smeared through the wet left-side windows, is the rim and fill; shadows fall to deep teal-black but keep detail; no studio fill, no flat even lighting. The only extra light sources allowed are the ones the shot description names (the green glow of a phone screen, white headlights through the rear window). Colour grade: deep teal shadows against orange and red highlights, muted mid-tone saturation, skin stays a true warm brown, blacks very slightly lifted. Lens: spherical prime look, 35 mm for wider cabin shots, 50 mm for mediums, 85 mm for close-ups, near f/2 with shallow depth of field, soft round bokeh from raindrops on glass, gentle halation around bright lights, slight natural vignette. Camera at seated eye level inside the cramped cabin, steady framing, level horizon, no wide-angle distortion. Fine 35 mm film grain over the whole frame. Rain is always present: beads and runnels on every window, wet reflections on vinyl, leather and skin. Composed for vertical video: one clear subject, the main face in the upper-middle of the frame, the bottom fifth of the frame free of faces and essential action, and a little spare picture on all four edges so the frame can be slowly pushed in or panned.
look.negativeRules: AVOID: No text of any kind anywhere in the image: no captions, subtitles, titles, labels, signage lettering, number plates, permit stickers, meter digits, phone-screen characters, readable newsprint or headlines; any printed surface is blurred or illegible. No watermarks, signatures, logos, brand names, borders, frames or split panels. No real company, bank, police, government or taxi-union insignia or emblems, no flags, no real or recognisable people. No extra people beyond those named in the shot, no faces in other vehicles. Do not change any character's face, age, skin tone, hair, wardrobe or jewellery from the reference sheet; do not add earrings, bindi, glasses, cap, watch, rings, moustache or beard. Right-hand-drive car only: the steering wheel and the driver are on the right side of the car. No extra, missing or fused fingers, no distorted hands, no duplicated limbs. No illustration, anime, cartoon, 3D render, CGI gloss, HDR glow, plastic skin, beauty filter or over-saturated colour. No daylight, no dry windows, no weapons, no blood.

notes: Nine shots, 31.7 s. Tara's sheet is attached, first, to seven of them (all but s02 and s07). Her face is the subject of six (s01, s03, s04, s05, s06, s09): front-on, low angle with green uplight, right profile, extreme close-up, wider with a foreground blur, and backlit near-silhouette. s08 uses the sheet for her hand and sleeve only.

Imran is a voice only until s06. He is first seen, out of focus, on the word driver, and his eyes are first seen in the mirror in s07. The script puts his eyes in the mirror in b1 and b3 as well; with a nine-shot ceiling those two mirror cutaways were dropped so that b6 could keep both the mirror and the door lock.
The script cuts back to Tara for the grin dying at the end of b2. Here the insert holds for all of b2 with her whisper over it, and the dead grin is delivered by s03 under the green phone light.
b4 is cut in two on the interruption (end of l06, start of l07) so neither half runs past 5 s. The longest shot is s06 at 6.0 s (the whole of l08), played as one continuous push-in.

Key props (duffel bag, keypad phone, bag contents) are described in words in every prompt, copied from style.json key_props, and are not attached as images: the brief for this file limits refs to character sheets and location plates, three at most. If props drift between s01, s02, s03 and s09, the first fix is to add duffel_bag, bag_contents or keypad_phone as an extra reference and label it in the prompt.

Door-lock knobs are UP in s01, s03, s04, s06 and s07 and DOWN in s08 and s09. Wipers are still in s07 and never move in any shot: the b7 wiper sweep was cut from the script. The phone screen is never shown lit to camera.

Stills cannot lip-sync, so lines are kept off moving mouths where possible: l02, l04 and l10 are Imran off-screen; l05, l07 and l08 are the unseen caller; of Tara's four lines, l03 plays over the bag insert and l09 over the hand insert, and only l01 (mid-laugh) and l06 (profile, lips just parted) play on her face.

Continuity keeper (S4): the plate labels in s03, s08 and s09 said 'Match them exactly' while the plates show lock knobs UP, sedan lights off and no green glow. Each now names its exception (s03 green phone glow; s08 knob DOWN; s09 knob DOWN and headlights on behind) so the reference does not override the shot. See continuity.json.

Storyboard revision (S7) after the script rewrite: total 31.7 s (s06 goes from 4.8 to 6.0 s for l08's new target); action text re-quoted from the current script (l03, l04, l07, l08); s01 has her already pulling the zip and is no longer out of breath; the wiper sweep is gone from s09; s02 no longer says 'No people' while showing her lap. Line ids, beat ids, refs, light states and the nine-shot order are unchanged. See review-notes.json storyboard_fixes.

Screen-direction map (S7): the scene's line runs from Tara (rear left) to Imran (front right). Every frontal camera (s01, s03, s05, s06, s09) sits at the front of the cabin on the kerb side of that line: the driver is frame left, the neon door window is frame right, and the phone at her right ear is on the left of her face as we see it. s07 is her point of view along the line (driver frame right, a normal reverse). s04 and the s08 insert look across from the rear-right seat, which is the far side of the line: in s04 the front of the car is frame right. s04 stays there because the script's b4 image (right profile, phone visible at her ear, neon window behind her) can only be seen from that side. It is entered from s03 and left through s05, both frontal with her eyes down and no sideways look, and s06 then re-establishes the driver at frame left. Do not add a sideways eye-line to s03, s04 or s05.

shots.prompt: Use your image generation tool to create ONE new vertical 9:16 image. REFERENCES, in the order attached: Image 1 is the character reference sheet for Tara. The woman in this shot is that exact person: same face and bone structure, skin tone, hair, kajal, nose stud, gold chain, blazer and blouse. Use the sheet only for who she is and what she wears; do not copy its grey studio background, its flat white light, its poses or its multi-view layout. Image 2 is the location plate of this taxi's cabin looking back at the rear-left seat. The cabin in this shot is that exact cabin: same teal-green seat vinyl and wear, door hardware, headliner, windows, outside world, rain and light. Match them exactly. SHOT: Eyeline first, in frame terms, because it is the most important instruction in this shot: Tara's head and eyes are turned slightly towards FRAME LEFT; she is looking just past the left edge of the lens at the unseen driver, who sits beside the camera on the LEFT side of the picture. She is NOT looking at the neon window on frame right, not looking out of any window and not looking into the camera; the neon is behind her at the right edge of the picture and she ignores it. (The camera looks backwards down the car, so the driver's side of the car is the left side of the picture and the kerb-side neon window is the right side of the picture.) Medium close-up of Tara, front-on, 50 mm lens, camera between the two front seat-backs at seated eye level, looking back at her on the rear-left seat (the same direction as the location plate, but closer). She is rain-damp and still wired with adrenaline from the job she has just pulled off: mid-laugh, mouth open in a wide, triumphant, slightly disbelieving grin that shows her teeth, eyebrows up, eyes bright and alive. Her face is turned about 15 degrees towards frame left and both irises sit towards the frame-left corners of her eyes: the laugh is aimed at the driver off the left edge of the picture, never at the window on the right. Her head and shoulders lean slightly forward with adrenaline. Her hair is black, not brown: true jet black and wet, and it stays black under the orange street light, which adds only thin orange highlights on a few wet strands. She is 31 and looks 31: even in the wide grin her laugh lines and the creases at the corners of her eyes are light and shallow and her skin is firm; do not age her. A tan leather duffel bag stands on her lap, bulging and heavy, still shut. Both her hands are at its brass zip: her left hand grips the top of the bag right beside the zip, close to her right hand and near the vertical centre line of the frame, holding the leather taut (it is not out at the end of the bag); the thumb and forefinger of her right hand pinch the brass pull tab and have just started to drag it, so the first few centimetres of zip teeth behind the pull have parted into a thin dark slit. Both hands are close together in front of her body, elbows tucked in. The bag is otherwise closed and nothing inside it can be seen. Fresh raindrops sit on her hair and on the dark, wet shoulders of her blazer. Behind her: the worn teal-green vinyl seat-back, the rain-covered rear window at upper left, and at frame right the rear-left door window with red and blue neon smeared through the running rain; the small chrome lock knob on that window sill stands UP. The engine is off. Nobody else is visible. LIGHT: Base light state. The warm sodium-orange street light through the windscreen is the key: it comes from the camera side, slightly from frame left, across her face. Red and blue neon through the rear-left door window at frame right is the rim: along her tucked left ear, cheekbone, jaw line and the wet shoulder of her blazer. Shadows fall to deep teal-black but keep detail. No other light source. COMPOSITION: Her face is in the upper-middle of the frame with a little headroom. The top of the bag and both her hands sit about two-thirds of the way down. The lowest quarter of the frame shows only the tan leather body of the bag and dark seat. Both her hands, both wrists, the brass pull tab and the parted stretch of the zip sit inside the central 80 percent of the frame width: no finger, knuckle or wrist is in the outer 10 percent of the frame on the left or on the right. Only the plain leather ends of the bag may run out towards the side edges. logline.en: Two a.m. at Jalebiganj thana: the malkhana locker is empty. Twenty lakh in seized cash is gone, and in its place sits one motichoor laddoo. The lock isn't broken, there are only two keys, and one of them is in Sub-Inspector Meenu Rawat's pocket.

story.location: Malkhana (case-property store room) of the fictional Jalebiganj Police thana: a cramped back room with a grey steel almirah-style locker, shelves of tagged bundles and dented trunks, a wooden desk with a ledger and a phone lying face up (Meenu's own phone, left there when she went for chai), a slow ceiling fan, one bare tungsten bulb in the corridor behind the doorway. No flags, no national emblems, no portraits.
story.timeOfDay: Night, about 2 a.m. The room is dark except for the torch beam and warm corridor light from the doorway.

characters.look: Lean, upright, medium-brown skin. Black hair in a tight low bun with one loose strand falling over the left temple. Thick straight eyebrows, a small mole under the right eye, tired sharp eyes. Khaki full-sleeve uniform shirt with sleeves rolled to the elbow, dark teal epaulettes with two plain white bars, a round teal shoulder patch showing a white lantern (the fictional Jalebiganj Police emblem), black belt, a steel-strap wristwatch on the left wrist. No cap. Carries a small ring with one long brass key.
characters.note: Low-mid female voice, dry and clipped, north-Indian small-town Indian English (same actor as the Hinglish cut). Tired authority; gets quieter, not louder, when she is actually scared. Fast on the short lines.

characters.look: Short and round with a pot belly, lighter brown skin, thick salt-and-pepper handlebar moustache, round cheeks, receding hairline. Khaki uniform with the same teal epaulettes (no bars) and lantern shoulder patch, a maroon sleeveless sweater-vest pulled over the shirt, a grey muffler round the neck. Holds a chunky yellow plastic torch in his right hand at all times.
characters.note: Warm, slightly nasal male tenor, eager to please, Hindi-medium Indian English with the grammar left as he would say it. Speaks a beat too slowly when delivering bad news and trails off. Earnest, never joking: the comedy is that he means it.

endingQuestion.hi: The officer who holds the only other key is on leave, so why is he calling at 2 a.m., the very minute the empty locker is found, and will Meenu pick up?

Two frames. Cut on Meenu crossing the room (off-screen: the chai glass clinks down on the steel rack and she shoves Bablu's torch hand up to aim it herself). Frame 1, INSERT, torch-lit: the bare middle shelf where the cash bundles were; one orange motichoor laddoo sits on a small paper plate. One second of silence on the laddoo, then l04 plays over it. Frame 2: close-up of Meenu staring down at it. l05 is hers; l06 plays off-screen over her unmoving face until the next shot cuts him off mid-word.
Meenu cuts him off, turning on him. Medium two-shot, her finger almost on his chest; Bablu leans back, torch beam swinging up to the ceiling fan.

One tall close frame built for a tilt: low in frame, Meenu's left hand (steel wristwatch) lifts the heavy brass padlock hanging open on the locker hasp and turns it in the torchlight, not a scratch on it; her face is above it, looking down. The camera tilts up from the lock to her face as the anger drains and she works it out. The first half of l08 lands on the padlock, the whispered half on her face.

One readable frame, held: Meenu has drawn the key ring from her trouser pocket and the single long brass key lies on her open right palm, catching the torch. Bablu is already half a step back, looking not at the key but at her. He counts the keys aloud, she finishes his sentence quietly (voiced, not whispered), and his last line is cut off by the phone.

SILENT BEAT. A phone buzzes. INSERT: Meenu's phone face up on the wooden desk beside the ledger, vibrating, its screen the only cold light in the room. Incoming call, contact photo of a heavy-set man in aviator sunglasses. The caller name "Bada Sahab" is added as an overlay in assembly, not painted into the frame. The music stops dead on the first buzz.

Tight close-up on Meenu, lit blue-white from below by the phone, the key clenched in her right fist. Bablu is a soft shape behind her shoulder. She does not reach for the phone. She asks the question in a low, clear, fully voiced tone (not a whisper), in the gap between two buzz pulses. Hold on her face one beat after the line, the buzz still going. Cut to black mid-buzz.

Sub-scores: hook 8, stakes 8, cliffhanger 8, natural Hinglish 8, performability 7, length 7.5, lead coverage 9.5 (overall 8.0). CLARITY (medium): two off-screen superiors are introduced in 30 seconds with nothing to separate them: 'DSP' (l07, inspecting at 9 a.m.) and 'बड़े साहब' (l10, on leave, the caller). In thana speech 'बड़े साहब' can mean either the SHO or the DSP/SP, so a cold viewer can read them as one man, which makes 'inspection at 9' contradict 'on leave' and muddies the cliffhanger.

LENGTH (medium): the 30.3 s total assumes zero gap between the 11 speaker changes and optimistic per-line targets. l08 is the worst: 15 syllables with an ellipsis and a half-whispered clause budgeted at 3.2 s (14.4 chars/s, fastest in the script, though whispering is slower); realistic 3.8-4.4 s. l05 gives 1.0 s for a sigh plus a word. His pivotal turn at l09 (he realises the key holder is standing in front of him) and l11 are untagged, and tags do not carry across turns in the dialogue endpoint, so the 'half step back' suspicion beat is likely to be read neutral. l06 ('मोतीचूर का है, mad—') depends entirely on an earnest read and has no tag.
